# ar-1 -- the site access point (#30).
#
# interface is the real radio, moved into this container's own network
# namespace by the "interfaces" list in this recipe. It is a netdev
# passthrough, not a USB device passthrough: a wireless adapter is
# claimed by its driver on the host, and what a container needs is the
# resulting interface, not the USB endpoint (daemon/src/device.c says
# so in as many words).
#
# bridge is the whole reason ADR-0264 exists. hostapd puts wlan0 into
# br0 and will create br0 if it is missing -- but it knows nothing
# about this container's other interfaces and would never enslave one,
# so a bridge hostapd built alone would carry the radio and nothing
# else. Cix builds br0 first, with the access-network veth already in
# it, and hostapd then adds the radio to the bridge it finds. Wireless
# clients and the wired access segment are one layer-2 domain.
#
# ctrl_interface is what the hostapd_cli console attaches to.
#
interface=wlan0
bridge=br0
driver=nl80211
ctrl_interface=/run/hostapd

#
# NO COUNTRY CODE, AND THAT IS A MEASUREMENT.
#
# country_code=GB was here, with ieee80211d/ieee80211h alongside it.
# hostapd got as far as driving the radio and then died:
#
#   wlan0: interface state UNINITIALIZED->COUNTRY_UPDATE
#   Failed to set country code
#   wlan0: Unable to setup interface.
#
# Setting a country code requires the kernel to have loaded the
# regulatory database, and on this host it never does (#342) -- the
# wireless-regdb artifact is in the cix-firmware image, but cfg80211
# does not have it by the time it is asked for. Until that is fixed,
# asking for any country is asking for a failure to start.
#
# With no country code the kernel applies its built-in WORLD domain
# ("00"), which is the conservative choice rather than a permissive
# one: it is the most restrictive rule set the kernel has, and it is
# what the radio uses until something authoritative says otherwise.
#
# That choice decides the band below, so the two are one decision.
#
#
# Band and channel.
#
# 5 GHz, channel 36. The adapter is an RTL8822BU -- 802.11ac dual-band
# -- and channel 36 is the bottom of UNII-1, which is non-DFS in every
# common domain. A DFS channel would make the AP wait out a radar scan
# before it ever beacons, which is a poor thing to debug a first
# bring-up through.
#
# 2.4 GHz, channel 6 -- forced by the world domain above, not chosen
# for its own sake. The world regdomain marks every 5 GHz band NO-IR
# (no initiating radiation), which is exactly what an AP does, so no
# 5 GHz channel can beacon under it; 2.4 GHz channels 1-11 carry no
# such flag and can. The adapter is an RTL8822BU and is dual-band, so
# 5 GHz becomes available again the moment the regulatory database
# loads and a real country code can be set -- channel 36 and the VHT
# block above are what to restore, in that order.
#
# NO VHT (802.11ac) HERE, AND THAT IS A BUILD FACT RATHER THAN A CHOICE.
#
# hostapd rejected ieee80211ac, vht_oper_chwidth and
# vht_oper_centr_freq_seg0_idx as "unknown configuration item" and
# refused to start -- upstream's defconfig, which hostapd.recipe uses
# as-is, leaves CONFIG_IEEE80211AC commented out, so the binary has no
# VHT support compiled in. An unknown item is fatal to hostapd, not a
# warning, so these cannot simply be left in place hopefully.
#
# The AP therefore runs 802.11n (HT) on 5 GHz, which is a real working
# access point at lower maximum rates. Turning VHT on means enabling
# CONFIG_IEEE80211AC in hostapd.recipe and rebuilding the package and
# this image -- worth doing, and deliberately not done in the same
# change as first bring-up, because the open question this container
# exists to answer is whether rtw88 does USB AP mode at all.
#
hw_mode=g
channel=6
ieee80211n=1

#
# The network itself.
#
# WPA2-PSK with CCMP only. TKIP is not offered at all -- it is broken,
# and offering it as a fallback is how a network ends up negotiating it.
#
# The passphrase below is a secret placeholder in the committed
# recipe, substituted from the apply request rather than stored here.
# This file is in git; the passphrase is not, and never will be.
#
# The placeholder is deliberately not spelled out in this comment:
# cixd warns when a RENDERED container still contains the token prefix,
# and prose describing it trips that check exactly as a forgotten
# secret would. A warning that cries wolf at documentation is worse
# than no warning.
#
ssid=cix
wpa=2
wpa_key_mgmt=WPA-PSK
rsn_pairwise=CCMP
wpa_passphrase={{SECRET:WIFI_PASSPHRASE}}

# Clients talk to each other through the bridge, which is what a normal
# wireless LAN does. Set to 1 to isolate them from one another.
ap_isolate=0
